div.head: I Cn 22.3
div.ab: And on þam godcundan gebede syn VII gebedu; mid þam se ðe hit inweardlice gesingð, he geærndað to Gode sylfum ymbe æfre ælce neode, þe man beþearf aðor oððe for þysum life oððe for ðam toweardan.
⁊ on þam goddcundan gebede synd seofan gebeda; mid þam se þe hit inweardlice gesingþ, geærndað to Gode sylfum ymbe æfre ælce neode, þe man beþearf aðor for ðissum lyfe oððe for þam toweardum.
⁊ on þam godcundam gebede syn seofen gebedu; mid ðam se ðe hit inweardlice gesingð, he geærndað to Gode sylfum ymbe æfre ælce neode, ðe man beðearf aðor oððe for ðissum life oððe for ðam toweardan.
In qua VII petitiones sunt; et quisquis eam intimo corde cantabit, cum ipso Deo agit de quacumque necessitate uitę presentis et futurę.
⁊ on þam godcunda[n] gebede syn seofen gebedu mid ðam se ðe hit inweardlice gesingð he geærndað to Gode sylfum ymbe æfre ælce neode ðe man beðearf aðor oððe for ðissum life oððe for ðam toweardan.
And on þam godcundan gebede syn VII gebedu; mid þam se ðe hit inweardlice gesingð, he geærndað to Gode sylfum ymbe æfre ælce neode, þe man beþearf aðor oððe for þysum life oððe for ðam toweardan.

Und in diesem göttlichen Gebete sind sieben Bitten; durch sie wendet sich, wer es innig hersagt, an Gott selbst um jegliche Nothdurft, die man bedarf entweder für dieses oder für das zukünftige Leben.
And in that divine prayer there are seven petitions; with them, whoever sings it inwardly intercedes with God himself for every need that one has, either for this life or for the life to come.

And in that sacred prayer there are seven petitions, and he who recites it from the depths of his heart inwardly makes supplication thereby to God himself for everything of which a man has need, both for this life and for the life to come.

And in that holy prayer are seven entreaties; he who recites it in his soul pleads with God himself concerning all things which may be to a person’s benefit, both in this life and in the life to come.
div.note: In A the text begins S. 46 with the red heading ‘Cnutes lage’. Liebermann compares Wulfstan p. 21.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
